clusters.title: [Impact] win32k-wpf on Config1 - Win32k may change WPF windowing and DPI
clusters.body:
<!-- impact:win32k-wpf:Config1 -->

Impact analysis conducted on source code version:

- https://github.com/defrances/HostApplication - commit `22b249a754b849dac151e976b533f60994fc6098`

## Updates applicable for this product configuration

| Title | Package | CVEs | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Win32k Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability | [KB5099444](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-57095) | CVE-2026-57095 | Install - High Prio |
| Win32k Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability | [KB5099444](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-49805) | CVE-2026-49805 | Install - High Prio |
| Windows Win32k Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability | [KB5099444](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-50688) | CVE-2026-50688 | Install - High Prio |
| Windows Win32k Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability | [KB5099444](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-56176) | CVE-2026-56176 | Install - High Prio |
| Windows Win32k Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability | [KB5099536](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-54112) | CVE-2026-54112 | Install - High Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: `Config1` (`Config1`, `Config2`, … — never a synthetic station id)
- Model / role: `LabBench-L110` / `lab-analysis-workstation`
- Deployment group: `lab-ring-0`
- OS: `Windows 11 IoT Enterprise` build `10.0.26100.4200`
- Clinical criticality: `high`
- Network exposure: `restricted_lan`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `H` | `H` | `H` |
| Product | `M` | `M` | `M` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

WPF windowing on `MainWindow.xaml` (`UseWPF` in `HostApplication.csproj`) and per-monitor DPI in `app.manifest` (`dpiAware` true/pm, `PerMonitorV2`) depend on the host Win32k stack. CI publishes `--self-contained true` for `win-x64` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`); the KB does not replace bits inside the exe.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** The published single-file exe bundles the .NET 9 runtime and does not load Win32k from a separate product package; `OutputType=WinExe` still starts without this cumulative KB.
- **If we install: App may break.** Win32k and GDI path changes after install can alter WPF layout, focus, or DPI scaling exercised by `MainWindow.xaml` and `app.manifest` without changing the bundled runtime.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Local Win32k elevation-of-privilege flaws on the station remain; the WPF client can still launch and render using today's host drivers.
- **Compatibility: Compatible with the app.** `MainViewModel` and `MainWindow` already run on the lab build strings shown in `SystemInformationProvider.GetCurrent()` (`SystemInformation.cs`).

### Conclusions

Install is a station hardening step for the Win32k surface that WPF uses; it is not a substitute for shipping a new self-contained Host Application build.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

These rows patch Win32k and related kernel windowing CVEs in the Windows kernel. SBOM scan and source code scan show no Win32k import in product code; coupling is through WPF's use of the host stack (`MainWindow.xaml`, `app.manifest`), not a packaged dependency.

## Product Risk assessment

Product functions affected: WPF UI shell, status bar, and system-information panel. Notes and bulletin HTTPS use separate host paths. Install risk is regression of layout/DPI after reboot; skip risk is continued exposure of the station Win32k attack surface while the app keeps running.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- None. No documented test covers Win32k or WPF DPI automation in `docs/test-plan.md`.

### Gap Analysis

- No UI automation or per-monitor DPI regression tests are documented.

## Recommendation

Lab validation should treat the Updates table as **Install - High Prio** for this configuration while keeping Host Application release artifacts on the self-contained `win-x64` build from CI; this note does not authorize production deployment.

clusters.title: [Impact] KB5099444 on Config1 - Host NTFS driver backs NoteStore AppData I/O
clusters.body:
<!-- impact:ntfs-notes:Config1 -->

Impact analysis conducted on source code version:

- https://github.com/defrances/HostApplication - commit `22b249a754b849dac151e976b533f60994fc6098`

## Updates applicable for this product configuration

| Title | Package | CVEs | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows NTFS Remote Code Execution Vulnerability | [KB5099444](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-50448) | CVE-2026-50448 | Install - High Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: `Config1` (`Config1`, `Config2`, … — never a synthetic station id)
- Model / role: `LabBench-L110` / `lab-analysis-workstation`
- Deployment group: `lab-ring-0`
- OS: `Windows 11 IoT Enterprise` build `10.0.26100.4200`
- Clinical criticality: `high`
- Network exposure: `restricted_lan`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `H` | `L` | `M` |
| Product | `M` | `M` | `M` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

`NoteStore.cs` reads and writes `%AppData%\HostApplication\notes.txt` via `File.ReadAllText`, `File.WriteAllText`, and `Directory.CreateDirectory`. `MainViewModel` constructs `NoteStore(NoteStore.DefaultPath)` and calls `Save`/`Load`. Tests `TC-SMOKE-NOTES` and `TC-UNIT-NOTES-EMPTY` lock this contract.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** Notes persistence uses the .NET file APIs against the user profile volume; the app does not ship or load `ntfs.sys` as a product dependency.
- **If we install: App may break.** An NTFS servicing update can change metadata handling or ACL behavior for the profile path used by `NoteStore.Save`, requiring smoke re-check of note round-trip.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Station NTFS remote-code-execution class flaws in the host filter driver remain; `NoteStore` can still read/write notes on an unpatched volume.
- **Compatibility: Compatible with the app.** Current `main` note I/O already succeeds on lab NTFS volumes per `NoteStoreTests` temp-path patterns.

### Conclusions

This KB hardens the host NTFS stack that stores local notes; it does not patch the self-contained .NET runtime inside the published zip.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

This patch fixes NTFS driver CVEs in the Windows kernel file system. SBOM scan and source code scan show no NTFS driver dependency in the product; `NoteStore.cs` is the coupling through standard file I/O to `%AppData%\HostApplication\notes.txt`.

## Product Risk assessment

Product functions affected: local notes save/load and export backup (`ExportCopy`). Hazard if install regresses file creation on the profile volume. Skipping leaves host NTFS exposure on the workstation while note features may still operate.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- TC-SMOKE-NOTES — save then load round-trip guarded in `docs/test-plan.md`.
- TC-UNIT-NOTES-EMPTY — missing file loads empty.

### Gap Analysis

- None identified for file I/O; no test covers NTFS-driver-specific edge cases.

## Recommendation

Lab validation should treat the Updates table as **Install - High Prio** for this configuration while keeping Host Application release artifacts on the self-contained `win-x64` build from CI; this note does not authorize production deployment.

| DirectX Graphics Kernel Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability | [KB5099536](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-50375) | CVE-2026-50375 | Install - High Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: `Config1` (`Config1`, `Config2`, … — never a synthetic station id)
- Model / role: `LabBench-L110` / `lab-analysis-workstation`
- Deployment group: `lab-ring-0`
- OS: `Windows 11 IoT Enterprise` build `10.0.26100.4200`
- Clinical criticality: `high`
- Network exposure: `restricted_lan`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `H` | `H` | `H` |
| Product | `M` | `M` | `M` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

WPF in `MainWindow.xaml` composes through DWM/DirectX using `PerMonitorV2` awareness declared in `app.manifest`. DirectX graphics kernel and overlay-filter servicing rows touch the same desktop composition path as the product UI chrome and `StaticResource` brushes.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** The product does not embed DirectX kernel drivers; rendering relies on in-box Windows composition already present on the host.
- **If we install: App may break.** Graphics kernel or overlay-filter updates can change vsync, layering, or per-monitor scaling behavior visible in the WPF layout after reboot.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Station DWM/DirectX elevation flaws remain on the host while the WPF client can still start.
- **Compatibility: Compatible with the app.** Current `main` UI resources in `App.xaml` and layout in `MainWindow.xaml` already render on lab Windows 10/11 builds listed in the configuration table.

### Conclusions

Treat as a WPF visual regression watch item after station graphics servicing; it is not an application-runtime patch.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

These rows patch DirectX graphics kernel and overlay filter components in Windows. SBOM scan and source code scan show no DirectX package reference; coupling is through WPF composition (`MainWindow.xaml`, `app.manifest` `PerMonitorV2`).

## Product Risk assessment

Product functions affected: primary WPF window and themed controls. No clinical data pathways. Install may require visual smoke on multi-monitor labs; skip leaves graphics-kernel exposure on the station.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- None. No documented test covers DWM or DirectX composition in `docs/test-plan.md`.

### Gap Analysis

- No UI automation for rendering or multi-monitor DPI in the published test plan.

## Recommendation

Lab validation should treat the Updates table as **Install - High Prio** for this configuration while keeping Host Application release artifacts on the self-contained `win-x64` build from CI; this note does not authorize production deployment.

clusters.impact:
### Impacted Components

WPF in `MainWindow.xaml` composes through DWM/DirectX using `PerMonitorV2` awareness declared in `app.manifest`. DirectX graphics kernel and overlay-filter servicing rows touch the same desktop composition path as the product UI chrome and `StaticResource` brushes.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** The product does not embed DirectX kernel drivers; rendering relies on in-box Windows composition already present on the host.
- **If we install: App may break.** Graphics kernel or overlay-filter updates can change vsync, layering, or per-monitor scaling behavior visible in the WPF layout after reboot.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Station DWM/DirectX elevation flaws remain on the host while the WPF client can still start.
- **Compatibility: Compatible with the app.** Current `main` UI resources in `App.xaml` and layout in `MainWindow.xaml` already render on lab Windows 10/11 builds listed in the configuration table.

### Conclusions

Treat as a WPF visual regression watch item after station graphics servicing; it is not an application-runtime patch.

findings.title: Vendor bulletin HTTPS accepts any server certificate
findings.evidence: src/HostApplication.Core/InsecureVendorBulletinClient.cs: AcceptAnyServerCertificate returns true only when sslPolicyErrors == SslPolicyErrors.None; CreateTrustingHandler wires that callback; TC-REG-TLS-CALLBACK asserts rejection of invalid chains. Catalog/inputs MDS2-TLS still documents the old bypass; main code matches a met TLS control (inputs MDS2-NET met for the single outbound HTTPS path).

findings.title: Notes stored as plaintext in user AppData
findings.evidence: src/HostApplication.Core/NoteStore.cs writes UTF-8 plaintext under %AppData%\HostApplication\notes.txt with no network export; inputs MDS2-DATA met (local notes only, no PHI). Residual risk is host-account access to the file.

findings.title: No inbound network listener
findings.evidence: No TcpListener/HttpListener/Kestrel or bind usage in application source; architecture and inputs MDS2-NET met (optional outbound HTTPS GET only, no inbound ports).

os_kb_advice: Host OS KBs (including Schannel/TLS stack updates) remain a station-level recommendation and are not included in the HostApplication application zip.
After application release, continue to apply Windows updates on the host separately from the self-contained win-x64 package.
